artists.name: Abe Partridge
artists.bio: Abe Partridge is a heralded singer-songwriter, visual artist, storyteller, and documentarian based in Mobile, Alabama. Since his 2018 debut Cotton Fields and Blood for Days, he has toured relentlessly across the U.S. and Europe, with performances at major festivals and iconic rooms including 30A Songwriters Festival, Laurel Cove, The Bluebird Cafe, Eddie's Attic, and Duke's. He has appeared on syndicated NPR programs including Mountain Stage and Woodsongs Old Time Radio Hour, and recently toured with Matthew Sweet, Drivin' N Cryin', and Dar Williams in support of Love in the Dark. Partridge also co-created the Alabama Astronaut podcast documenting previously unrecorded songs from holiness and serpent-handling churches in Appalachia. Beyond music, he is an acclaimed visual artist whose work has appeared in galleries and notable private collections, including art connected to Dr. Sleep, Tyler Childers, Charlie Parr, and the Red Clay Strays. He is currently preparing a 2026 album produced by Steve Shelley of Sonic Youth.

artists.name: Elliott Devaughn
artists.bio:
Singer-songwriter and musician Elliott Devaughn was born and currently resides in Northeast Mississippi. Growing up surrounded by various types of music, she found herself particularly drawn to indie folk rock.

A chance encounter with Mississippi musician Jimbo Mathus inspired her to take progressive guitar lessons from him. This mentorship opened up more performing opportunities and led to a recording session at Zebra Ranch. Elliott credits Jimbo's guidance as a significant factor in her growth as an artist and continues to collaborate with him on her new songs.

In addition to her guitar training, Elliott is experimenting with other instruments, including synthesizers and drum machines. Most recently, she has taken up bass guitar to enhance her rhythm skills and become a more well-rounded multi-instrumentalist, ready to shine at upcoming music events.

Elliott's sound, a captivating blend of indie folk rock, is heavily influenced by iconic bands such as Sonic Youth, The Velvet Underground, and The Strokes. Elements of Stevie Nicks, Joni Mitchell, and Fiona Apple resonate in Elliott's clear, airy voice. As a passionate Mississippi musician, she strives to discover more diverse sounds to enrich her ever-growing and unique tone.

At the beginning of 2025, Elliott fully immersed herself in her music career. In April 2025, her song "Fell in Love Too Fast" won first place at the University of North Alabama's songwriter competition. She is actively booking music events and is planning to record more songs later in the year. Performed at PorchFest 2026.

artists.name: Hayden Hunter & The Yearly Trials
artists.bio: Hayden Hunter and the Yearly Trials blend heartfelt songwriting with rootsy, road-worn instrumentation — a sound shaped by long nights, longer drives, and the stories picked up along the way. Drawing on Americana, indie folk, and alt-country influences, their music balances raw vulnerability with grounded, unshakable grit. Led by singer-songwriter Hayden Hunter, the band delivers lyrics that dig deep and arrangements that hit home. From intimate acoustic ballads to full-band anthems, their songs explore love, loss, change, and the quiet moments in between. Hometown: Jackson, Mississippi. Genres: Southern Alternative Rock. Performed at PorchFest 2026!

artists.name: Hope MacGregor
artists.bio:
Hope MacGregor is a songwriter, storyteller, artist, and Army Aviation Veteran. After eight years of active duty military service, Hope put down her uniform and found herself in law school. Then, in the middle of the global pandemic and the middle of school, her car broke down, her grandmother died, her dog got cancer, and her husband ran off with a blonde to Texas. With the encouragement of her father, MacGregor picked up her old guitar and pen – she started writing songs.

After graduating law school, Hope moved to Jackson, Tennessee where she found a town full of the best kind of music scene: one full of talented, authentic artists that support and care about one another. In short order she put together a band and over the last few years has released two studio albums, toured nationally, been featured on music festival line ups with Grammy-award winning artists, and was recently named a Rising Star in Tennessee music by the Tennessee Entertainment Commission!

Hope's music is a unique blend of Americana, blues, country, and honesty. She knows how to speak to the most tender parts of life with songs like Why Dogs and For Now. But it is MacGregor's own brand of take-no-crap humor in her writing, with songs like Screwed and Sloppy Seconds, that keeps folks coming back for more. If you want to get to know Hope, just ask her about her beloved yellow lab, Lucy.

artists.name: Huey
artists.bio: Huey (Atlanta, GA) writes Southern folk with jazz and indie edges—solo and with Huey & The Heaven-sent. Atwood Magazine has highlighted how she stretches what people expect from Southern music, especially around the band's second LP, How to Keep Things Alive. Her NPR Tiny Desk Contest entry "Buy In" drew national attention. Fellowships and residencies—including Slough Farm on Martha's Vineyard and Chalk Hill in Napa Valley—fed songs like Passerby and Chimes, while she works toward a psych-folk solo EP targeted for early 2027. Tour dates, merch, donate, and booking all live on huey-music.com.

artists.name: Janet Simpson
artists.bio:
Janet Simpson is a Birmingham-bred singer, guitarist, and keyboardist — a deep listener and collaborator across Wooden Wand (World War IV), Delicate Cutters, Teen Getaway, and Timber, her duo with Will Stewart (who also anchors her solo band).

Her solo debut Safe Distance (2021) set a high bar; Can I See You Tonight?, out September 19, 2025 via Cornelius Chapel, widens a wry, haunted alt-country lens with Jody Nelson, David Somerall, and Shawn Avery. The album was tracked at Cypress Moon Studios on the Tennessee River, where Brad Timko captured the room's Muscle Shoals lineage.

Her songs trade in longing, place, and the space between people.

artists.name: Jodie Ross
artists.bio: Jodie Ross is a Mississippi singer-songwriter from Louisville, shaped by southern gospel, Motown, classic rock, and country — with inspiration from Stevie Nicks, Melissa Etheridge, and Dolly Parton. Recognition includes a 2024 Josie Music Award nomination (Song of the Year), 2021 Mississippi Songwriter of the Year (People's Choice), and 2019 Mississippi Music Foundation Best Original Song of the Year. A former board-certified music therapist, she writes with empathy and grit; singles including "My Favorite Memory" are out now on streaming. Her official site is jodierossmusic.com.

artists.name: Joe A. MacGown
artists.bio:
Joe A. MacGown is a Mississippi artist who creates chaotic assemblages of strange mutated creatures, crowded surreal landscapes, and mandala-like designs that reflect his thoughts and observations of life on this planet. Using imaginative imagery and random patterns, he produces detailed drawings and mixed media paintings by simply allowing ideas to flow out of his head using a method he describes as "Subconscious Meandering." MacGown's background in entomology and natural history, coupled with his love of science fiction and cynicism of all things human, provide ample fodder for his surreal visions, which range from dark and foreboding to light and whimsical.

MacGown's work has been featured in numerous local and regional exhibitions as well as in international group shows in Dallas, TX; Chicago, IL; Memphis, TN; San Francisco, CA; Washington DC; Colombia; Toronto, Canada; Great Britain; the Philippines; Moscow and St. Petersburg, Russia; Belgrade, Serbia; the Netherlands; various venues in France; Dresden, Germany; Venice, Italy; Portugal; and other regions.

To see Joe's work or his son Joseph's work in person, contact Joe at art@joemacgown.com or text 662-418-5286 to schedule a visit to the MacGown Art Retreat and Studio (MARS) at 211 Sessums Road, Starkville, MS. Most weekday and Sunday afternoons from 1–6 pm are the best times to arrange a visit (by appointment only).

artists.name: Lance Cooper
artists.bio:
Hey friends! I'm Lance. I've been playing and supporting local music for over 20 years. I've performed solo for many years, as well as with AMFM and The Moves (formerly The Wright Moves). My love for music sparked when my older brother got a Les Paul—I was amazed. I slowly taught myself guitar at 13 and haven't put it down since.

I'm influenced by a lot of things. In my originals, I tend to write about my own life experiences. I cover a wide range of artists—The Avett Brothers, Ryan Adams, Dave Matthews, Goose, Prince, Ray LaMontagne, Counting Crows, and many more. I play what I love, and I'm inspired by life on a daily basis.

Music is my passion. Whether I'm listening, supporting, or playing, it fills my cup and keeps me wanting more. I always knew I wanted to be a musician and a father, and I've been blessed to become both—everything else is a bonus.

Come hang with me and enjoy yourself. You deserve it. Peace ✌️

artists.name: Megan Lea
artists.bio:
Megan Lea is committed to staying true. Born in Selma, Alabama and raised on a rural route, the importance of family, work ethic, and plenty of room for imagination were planted from the get-go. After years of sharing her original music on festival stages, in dive bars, and living rooms throughout the Southeast, those roots have grown into a sound all her own. These days, Megan lives a multifaceted life in many different roles; including Mama, ICU RN, Aunt, wife, bandmate, writer, and solo performing artist. The common thread among all of these is a self-aware sincerity and a burning curiosity for life that won't quit.

Megan's writing has been described as authentic, raw, soulful, and introspective, reminiscent of poetic storytellers like John Prine or Emmylou Harris. Her stage performances incorporate sincerity of connection with a raucous edge, especially when performing with her husband Brad, guitarist Andy Branton, and bassist Billy Rigdon as The Dirty Mirrors. Megan's textured vocal style, reminiscent of a Car Wheels Lucinda Williams with the simplicity of a Nebraska Springsteen adds an authenticity that turns listeners into believers.

"Whether we connect on the road, in the backyard, on the creek, onstage, or online, I'm grateful to share my world with you." —Megan Lea

Writes raw, emotional songs about loss, love, redemption, and addiction. Music featured on a Billboard Bluegrass Chart #11 album. Performed at PorchFest 2026.

artists.name: Shake It Like a Caveman
artists.bio: No stranger to the highway — a one man band dance party, thrusting somewhere between poolside film scores and early American work songs. Simultaneously playing slide guitar, harmonica, kick drum, kick snare, hi hat, and vocals. Sonic and visual dynamite that makes you move that thang. Formed in Tennessee in 2005, Shake It Like a Caveman currently performs worldwide at festivals, club dates, radio and TV. Performed at PorchFest 2026!

artists.name: Taylor Hollingsworth
artists.bio: Fingerpicking songwriter from Birmingham, AL, blending folk, rock, and blues into a style he calls "folk n' roll." Back with his latest album "Yahola," recorded at Dialback Sound in Water Valley, MS, Taylor stands apart as a true maverick of original music. His talent has earned him recognition from artists like Conor Oberst and Phoebe Bridgers, who covered one of his songs. Taylor has served as lead guitar player for Conor Oberst on worldwide tours and late-night TV appearances. Despite brushes with major labels, he walked away to maintain artistic freedom, prioritizing his family and his own vision. Founder of Dead Fingers alongside his wife, crafting tunes like "Ring Around Saturn" which hit nearly 3 million streams. His songs with The Blips earned "Coolest Song in the World" on Little Steven's Underground Garage. Whether playing intimate local bars, busking at farmers markets, or festival stages, Taylor's music tells stories that resonate deeply. Hometown: Birmingham, Alabama. Genres: Folk N Roll. Performed at PorchFest 2026!

artists.name: The Kites
artists.bio: THE KITES are an indie pop band from Oxford, MS. Inspired by jangle rock and modern pop, their energetic, catchy tunes will make you move and get stuck in your head.

artists.name: The Stifftones
artists.bio: What started as a Goonie adventure in 2019 has become the journey of a lifetime. Since 2021 The Stifftones have been traveling the US living in their 1996 Cadillac Hearse named Tania with their two dogs. Logging over 200,000 miles, they have performed hundreds of shows in almost as many towns. Shaun and Rachel Stief are a dynamic duo whose sound is a unique fusion of influences captivating audiences with their vocal harmonies and guitar weaves. Hailing from the heartland, their music embodies a mix of Midwest meets Bakersfield country, a dash of East Coast flair, and a healthy dose of good ol' Rock and Roll, all wrapped in magic. Hometown: Greenville, Illinois. Performed at PorchFest 2026!

artists.name: The Moves

artists.name: Too Darn Loud
artists.bio: Too Darn Loud is an oddball alt/rock duo from Mississippi featuring Isaac Hitt (Guitar & Noises) and Brandon Goehner (Percussion & Vocals). They performed at PorchFest 2026 on Saturday, with new releases "Nothing To Do" and "Sophisticated 60s Sci-Fi" streaming now.

artists.name: Tyler Tisdale
artists.bio: Master of Americana music, weaves the soul of the heartland into every note. His melodies resonate like the echoes of open fields, and his lyrics paint a vivid canvas of American stories. Performed at PorchFest 2026.
